subject: Numeracy
title: Counting objects to 10
subtopics: Counting in a line and a circle
objectives: Children will touch each object once as they count to 10.
Children will say the last number as how many.
content: Touching each object once, counting in a line and a circle, and saying how many there are.
teachingActivities: Teach the one-to-one rule: touch, move and say; arrange objects in a line first, then a circle, then a scatter; always ask "How many are there?" after counting; use tricks such as moving counted items into a box.
learnerActivities: Count up to 10 objects with one-to-one touch and say how many.
assessment: Observe whether each child counts up to 10 objects accurately and says how many.
expectedOutcomes: Counts up to 10 objects with one-to-one touch.
Says how many in a group.

lessons.title: Touch each one
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will touch each object once while counting to ten.
successCriteria: Does not miss or repeat objects
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say numbers to 10 and count up to 5 objects.
lessons.starter: Show ten counters in a line and say "We touch each one once. We do not miss any."
teacherActivities: Touch each counter and move it to a plate as you count.
Show what happens if you count one twice.
Let each child count a line of counters.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Touch each counter and move it to a plate as you count. Children: Children count aloud with you.
Step 2. Teacher: Show what happens if you count one twice. Children: Children say oops and laugh.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child count a line of counters. Children: Child touches and counts.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "How many?" after each count. Children: Child says the last number.

practical.title: Touch and move
practical.safety: Use counters too large to swallow. Keep children seated and supervise closely.

differentiation.support: Count up to five with the child touching and moving.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count ten counters and then fifteen.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we do to each one?

lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say "Ten."
lessons.homeConnection: Count ten pegs or spoons together, touching each once.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "touch each object once while counting to ten" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting in a circle
lessons.subject: Numeracy
lessons.subtopic: Counting in a line and a circle
objectives: Children will count objects arranged in a circle.
successCriteria: Starts and stops at the same place
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say numbers to 10 and count up to 5 objects.
lessons.starter: Make a circle of counters and say "In a circle, where do we start? We need a marker."
teacherActivities: Put a coloured counter as a marker and count from there.
Show how to stop at the marker.
Let each child count a circle of counters.
Compare a circle count and a line count.
learnerActivities: Child counts and stops at the marker.
Child says the numbers are the same.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Put a coloured counter as a marker and count from there. Children: Children count with the teacher.
Step 2. Teacher: Show how to stop at the marker. Children: Children watch and say stop.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child count a circle of counters. Children: Child counts and stops at the marker.
Step 4. Teacher: Compare a circle count and a line count. Children: Child says the numbers are the same.

practical.title: Circle count
practical.safety: Use large counters and supervise counting. Keep the floor clear.

differentiation.support: Count a circle of five with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count a circle of twelve.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Starts and stops at the marker
lessons.conclusion: Put the counters away and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Count items arranged in a circle at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count objects arranged in a circle" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: How many are there?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count groups and say how many are there.
successCriteria: Says how many in a group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say numbers to 10 and count up to 5 objects.
lessons.starter: Show a basket of objects and say "How many are there? Let us find out."
teacherActivities: Count the objects together and say how many.
Put a numeral card by the group.
Give each child a basket to count.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Count the objects together and say how many. Children: Children count aloud.
Step 2. Teacher: Put a numeral card by the group. Children: Child matches a card.
Step 3. Teacher: Give each child a basket to count. Children: Child counts the basket.
Step 4. Teacher: Swap baskets and count again. Children: Child counts a new basket.

practical.title: Count the basket
practical.safety: Use only large objects and keep small items out of reach. Supervise baskets.

differentiation.support: Use a basket of five or fewer objects.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a basket with more than ten.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

expectedOutcomes: Says how many in a group
lessons.conclusion: Return the baskets and say the numbers.
lessons.homeConnection: Count a group of objects and say how many.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count groups and say how many are there" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Counting scattered things
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will count scattered objects by moving them as they count.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say numbers to 10 and count up to 5 objects.
lessons.starter: Scatter stones on the mat and say "Now they are everywhere. How can we count them?"
teacherActivities: Show how to move each stone into a basket as you count.
Let children count the scattered stones.
learnerActivities: Child moves and counts each stone.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show how to move each stone into a basket as you count. Children: Children watch.
Step 2. Teacher: Let children count the scattered stones. Children: Child moves and counts each stone.
Step 3. Teacher: Ask "How many?" and compare. Children: Child says the number.
Step 4. Teacher: Count again to check. Children: Child counts again.

practical.title: Scatter and count
steps: Move each one to a basket.
practical.safety: Use stones larger than a child’s fist and wash hands afterwards. Check for sharp edges first.

differentiation.extension: Ask the child to count two baskets and say the total.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do you not lose count?

expectedOutcomes: Moves objects as they are counted
lessons.conclusion: Put the stones away and wash hands.
lessons.homeConnection: Scatter small safe objects and count them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "count scattered objects by moving them as they count" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 3 counting objects check
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Teachers will observe how accurately each child counts objects.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can say numbers to 10 and count up to 5 objects.
lessons.starter: Sing the counting rhyme and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: line, circle and scatter.
At each station ask "How many?" and watch.
Record each child’s level and highest accurate count.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: line, circle and scatter. Children: Children rotate every five minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How many?" and watch. Children: Child counts and answers.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and highest accurate count. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Counting stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and use large counters. Keep floors clear.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use groups up to five.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to count to twenty.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: touches each object once; counts in a line; counts in a circle; counts scattered objects; says how many.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 3
lessons.conclusion: Wave goodbye and say well done.
lessons.homeConnection: Keep counting objects at home every day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how accurately each child counts objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
